NMPolitics.net, August 2, 2006: 'Gov. Bill Richardson has declared a state of disaster in eight counties' (Dona Ana, Grant, Hidalgo, Sandoval, San Miguel, Sierra, Socorro and Valencia) after a week of heavy rain and thunderstorms. The story does not give the day he signed, so the row carries the date of the report.
Eastern New Mexico News, March 26, 2007: 'Gov. Bill Richardson declared Clovis a state disaster area Sunday' (March 25) and released $750,000 by executive order, after Friday's tornado.

Insurance Journal (AP), August 11, 2008: 'Richardson has declared Lincoln and Otero counties disaster areas' after the July 27 flood from the remnants of Hurricane Dolly. The story does not give the day he signed, so the row carries the date of the report.
Mountain Mail (Socorro), August 19, 2010: the Governor signed the disaster order on Tuesday, August 17, for flood damage after heavy rains in late July and early August.
KRWG, February 3, 2011: Gov. Susana Martinez 'has declared a state of emergency' after thousands lost natural gas service in the bitter cold that began Tuesday, February 1.
Los Alamos Daily Post, reprinting Executive Order 2013-029, signed July 30, 2013: 'declaring an emergency throughout New Mexico due to the severe storms and flooding across the state in July'.

Los Alamos Daily Post, reprinting Executive Order 2013-031: 'do hereby declare a State of Disaster to exist in state of New Mexico due to flooding', with the emergency period starting September 9, 2013. The order as printed carries no signing date; the Associated Press reported Gov. Martinez declared the emergency on Friday, September 13, 2013 (https://www.fox13now.com/2013/09/13/new-mexico-floods-hundreds-evacuated-governor-declares-emergency).
